Description: INSERM NOUVELLE-AQUITAINE REGIONAL DELEGATION STRUCTURE - UMR 1219 DIRECTED BY M. THIEBAUT The SISTM team, led by Mélanie Prague, is part of the Inserm U1219 Bordeaux Population Health Center (BPH). https://www.bordeaux-population-health.center/the-teams/biostatistics/ MAIN MISSION The recruited person will have the mission of participating in the construction of mathematical models (based on differential equations) of the immune response induced by vaccination and viral dynamics after infection by helping to integrate the latest known biological results in virology and immunology in this area. This project will take place within the framework of the PEPR MIE Previx. This project is structured into six working groups using quantitative approaches adapted to the diversity of data generated in the context of a pandemic. The objective is to define the microbiological, infectious disease and epidemiological contours of future threats. The project will develop methods to detect, characterize and model a new pathogen in real time from the first available information. It will notably deal with the analysis of heterogeneous data and the use of machine learning. The consortium brings together nine research units with interdisciplinary skills. It will produce knowledge useful to public health and will contribute to the training of a new generation of specialists capable of anticipating respiratory virus X. As part of this project, the contract researcher will integrate into the intra-host work package. A first contribution will be to investigate innovative and optimal preclinical trial designs in collaboration with Jeremie Guedj and France Mentre from the Inserm IAME Paris unit. One of the challenges will be the development of optimal designs to obtain reliable estimates of viroimmunological parameters in experimental models in non-human primates. These models are essential for the study of viral pathogenesis and therapeutic strategies. Estimating these parameters, however, remains difficult due to resource constraints and experimental design. The work will focus on the use of simulations to analyze the impact of different inoculation doses and increased heterogeneity in the timing of interventions, in order to improve the robustness of estimates and the ability to identify correlates of protection.
